stories.title: Plea to give Thames seals space for everyone's safety
stories.summary: Marmalade the harbour seal was a familiar visitor to the River Thames, often popping up at Greenwich and Rotherhithe in south-east London. She was given her nickname because of her bright golden-coloured coat. However, as the number of seal sightings along the river increases, charity Thames Seal Watch has urged members of the public to give the animals space. Despite looking cute, Emma Kelly from the charity says: "They can bite and they carry zoonotic diseases which are not very pleasant if you were to suffer a bite. "They will do that to protect themselves." She says getting close to the animals can cause them distress and stress, which could lead to their death. The charity says more and more of the seals are travelling further up the river, with one spotted as far west as Windsor. It is thought there are about 3,500 seals living in the Thames and that they mostly stay around the estuary, east of London. Marmalade was considered rare because there are only 500 harbour seals living in the river, compared with about 3,000 of the more common grey seals. Gareth Richards from UK Seal Alliance says "seals are very transient, and will basically go to where there is good fish stocks". He says "seals can swim from anything between 60 and 80 miles a day". Because they are being spotted more frequently, Richards says he would like to see further protection of the animals in law.

stories.headline: Malaysia’s PAS eyes new pecking order as it rekindles ties with Umno

opening: Malaysia’s biggest Islamist opposition party has used its annual convention to reopen the door to former rival Umno, while signalling that any reunion will come with a new pecking order as the party sets its sights on leading the federal government.

The recalibration comes after a partnership involving Umno and the Pan-Malaysian Islamic Party (PAS) jointly toppled Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s coalition in Negeri Sembilan last month, weeks after Umno crushed Pakatan Harapan (PH) in Johor.
